controls.reason: A record can state an accessibility target, but deciding which standard, version, and conformance level is actually required needs accessibility and often legal authority.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The record says WCAG 2.1 A while the product's jurisdiction and procurement contract require WCAG 2.2 AA. All three fields pass although the required target is not documented.

controls.reason: The statement is limited to whether the approved automated scans meet a numeric approved threshold, which bound scan artifacts and scope joins decide exactly.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a missing page result, stale artifact, wrong threshold, and score below threshold; each fails the bound inventory or comparison. Manual accessibility quality is outside this scan-result-only claim.

controls.reason: Identifying every meaningful visual element and its applicable contrast treatment requires semantic and accessibility judgment beyond numeric color comparisons.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An icon conveys payment failure only through color but is marked decorative and omitted from the meaningful-element inventory. All measured items meet ratios while the control remains violated.

controls.reason: Markup can be compared with a locale map, but whether each dynamic or mixed-language region has the correct language and direction is semantic and scope-dependent.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An Arabic page contains an unmarked English product-name passage and a user-generated Hebrew segment with wrong direction. The page-level `lang` and `dir` match the declared locale, so the proposed check passes.

controls.reason: A defect register cannot prove it contains every accessibility defect, and severity and meaningful regression coverage require specialist judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A keyboard trap is never entered in the register; every listed defect has an owner, severity, date, and a trivial regression test. The schema passes while an unowned serious defect remains.

controls.reason: The support inventory defines its own scope and cannot independently prove every locale, script, zone, currency, or region actually offered by code, configuration, content, or contracts.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Runtime configuration enables a Croatian locale and euro pricing for a region omitted from the record. Every declared support entry is documented, so the universal documentation check passes.

controls.reason: The claim is that two named content-direction categories are tested, not that all layouts are correct; authenticated executions bound to both categories prove that occurrence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an RTL-only run, a mixed-direction case without execution, and evidence for another revision; each fails. Visual quality outside the recorded oracle is not asserted.

controls.reason: A finite locale matrix cannot exhaust the values, calendars, plural categories, rounding contexts, and application meanings covered by eight broad correctness claims.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Fixtures pass for common positive values, but a negative currency amount and the Croatian few plural form render incorrectly. Every approved case passes while formatting is not generally correct.

controls.reason: Correct collation, search, tokenization, and case behavior depends on language context and an exhaustive corpus and oracle that the approved matrix does not define.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The suite covers ASCII words but Turkish dotted I search fails and a Japanese tokenizer splits names incorrectly. Approved cases pass while locale-specific behavior remains wrong.

controls.reason: A declared sensitive-field inventory cannot enumerate every serialization path, generated URL, signature input, token, identifier, and locale transformation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted export localizes a decimal inside a signed identifier. All declared fields remain byte-identical across locales, so the proposal passes while a security-sensitive form is altered.

controls.reason: Promise and schedule records can omit a language or period and do not prove assigned staff can actually provide support in that language.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A Croatian weekend promise is absent from the promise registry, and weekday coverage names a person who does not speak Croatian. All declared joins pass despite missing coverage.

controls.reason: Field presence and timestamps do not establish that the recorded goals are genuinely usability or quality-in-use goals or that interface selection occurred afterward.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A record created first says only `make it good`; a solution is then selected. Required fields and ordering pass, but no measurable usability goal was defined.

controls.reason: The statement is an exact research-recording requirement with five named fields, so an authenticated study record and evidence binding fully decide it.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting participant characteristics, recording no limitation, or linking evidence from another study; each fails the field or binding checks. Study quality is not claimed.

controls.reason: The proposal does not independently enumerate every fix needing user verification or define a complete user-study protocol and success oracle.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A navigation fix is omitted from the matrix and receives only design review, while a minor color fix has a user-test record. All declared scenarios pass although the rule is not followed for the navigation fix.

controls.reason: Repository configuration cannot prove all research artifacts are present, nor that provenance, access, and expiry remain enforced across exports and shadow copies.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A researcher keeps interview videos in an unlisted shared drive without expiry while every item in the official repository has correct metadata and permissions. The proposal passes.

controls.reason: Nonempty fields do not establish a coherent content hierarchy, navigable relationships, useful metadata, or appropriate search behavior.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The record lists arbitrary page IDs, calls every page top-level, and says search `default`. All five headings exist, but the product's information architecture is not meaningfully defined.

controls.reason: The content registry is not independently complete, so pages, campaigns, help articles, and generated content can evade ownership and lifecycle fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A live localized help article is absent from the registry and has no owner or review date. Every registered item has all five fields, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Whether interface states are perceptibly and semantically distinguishable requires visual and accessibility judgment, not only different state tokens or snapshots.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Selected, focused, and disabled buttons receive distinct class names but render identically to low-vision users. State-value comparisons pass while the states are not distinguishable.

controls.reason: State rows or mockups do not prove every relevant flow has a designed, coherent experience for all eight states, and design quality is semantic.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every state name appears in a design record, but the offline and recovery rows point to blank frames and an unlisted checkout component has no partial state. The schema passes.

controls.reason: Whether users, tasks, contexts, and thresholds are representative and severity is appropriate requires human research and product judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A study defines only expert desktop users for a consumer mobile product and labels them representative. Every field is present, so the record passes despite an unrepresentative plan.

controls.reason: Separate execution labels do not establish valid learnability and efficiency studies without defined participant cohorts, repetition, measures, and oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The first-use and repeated-use tests both use the same expert once and record page-load time as efficiency. Two executions exist, but neither meaningfully tests the claimed quality.

controls.reason: What counts as infrequent, stressful, high-stakes, and interruption-prone is contextual, and the proposal defines no valid human-study protocol for those conditions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A routine settings change is labelled all four categories and tested without interruption. The matrix is complete by label while actual high-stakes and interruption-prone tasks remain untested.

controls.reason: This control requires inclusion of two named contexts in usability evidence; authenticated study metadata can prove assistive-technology use and controlled low connectivity.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an ordinary-browser run labelled assistive, unrestricted networking labelled slow, and evidence from another revision; environment capture and study binding reject each. Broad usability success is not asserted.

controls.reason: An approved journey matrix can omit critical cross-boundary journeys, and end-to-end coverage across devices, channels, teams, and external services has no complete inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A password-recovery journey crosses email and support but is omitted; a trivial profile journey covers the approved matrix. Its execution passes while an actual cross-channel journey remains untested.

controls.reason: The requirement is to compare recorded outcomes with already defined objectives, so exact objective identifiers, formulas, observations, and comparison records decide it.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an outcome without an objective, an unmatched objective, and a comparison using another study's observation; exact set and scope joins fail each. Whether objectives are wise is separate.

controls.reason: The statement asks for six explicit design-system governance definitions, and a current authoritative record with those nonempty sections fully proves documentation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting consumers, leaving support policy blank, or naming no owner; each fails. The checker need not decide whether the chosen contribution model is optimal.

controls.reason: Section presence cannot establish usable examples, truthful accessibility behavior, or clear migration guidance, and applicable component scope may be omitted.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each component page contains the seven headings but uses `TBD` examples and falsely claims keyboard support. The record passes while the required documentation is not substantive.

controls.reason: Visual and semantic correctness, screen-reader meaning, and responsive quality lack exhaustive deterministic oracles even when every approved fixture executes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Snapshots match baselines, but a screen reader announces a destructive button as a link and a clipped translation is approved into the baseline. All fixture comparisons pass while two required behaviors fail.

controls.reason: The release inventory can omit a breaking change, and deciding material breakage and whether communication reached consumers before adoption requires contextual evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A token rename silently breaks a downstream theme but is labelled nonbreaking and omitted from notices. Every declared breaking change was communicated before its recorded adoption, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Materiality and whether an upgrade path is clear and usable are contextual; a nonempty link or nominal tool does not prove the requirement.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A material API change links to a one-line note saying `update code`, with no codemod or actionable steps. Record presence passes although no clear upgrade path is provided.

controls.reason: Metric-field presence does not prove that divergence, accessibility issues, maintenance cost, or user consistency are meaningfully measured.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A dashboard reports component download counts for all six labels and calls the same count user consistency. Every metric entry exists, but several required qualities are not measured.

controls.reason: Identifying duplicated or unsafe components and judging whether a migration is controlled require contextual and accessibility/security judgment, while inventories can omit components.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unsafe legacy date picker is excluded from the registry; another duplicated button has a plan containing only `later`. Required fields pass while unsafe duplication remains unmanaged.

controls.reason: A journey-test registry can omit journeys, and a passing execution does not establish that reuse was not substituted for meaningful usability and accessibility testing.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A team runs only component accessibility tests and records one trivial journey as complete. All declared evidence exists while checkout journey usability and accessibility were never evaluated.

controls.reason: The statement is a support-policy documentation requirement with six explicit matrix dimensions, which an authoritative versioned matrix can satisfy exactly.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a browser row without an operating system, a device without viewport bounds, and an assistive-technology entry with no input mode; each fails matrix completeness. Actual compatibility is not claimed.

controls.reason: Supporting zoom, reflow, spacing, orientation, and font preferences requires exhaustive visual and accessibility oracles across content, states, browsers, and sizes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The approved matrix covers the home page, but a long localized form loses controls at 400% zoom. All supplied executions pass while the product does not support zoom and reflow generally.

controls.reason: A scenario matrix cannot enumerate every function and interaction, and whether an alternative is equivalent and usable needs accessibility judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A canvas editor has a precision-only resize handle omitted from the matrix. Every declared hover and gesture action has a keyboard fixture, so the proposal passes while one function has no alternative.

controls.reason: The control requires tests under five named environmental conditions, not universal success; authenticated runs with exact resource and network settings prove occurrence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a normal-memory run labelled low-memory, latency without packet loss labelled intermittent, and stale evidence; captured environment parameters and revision binding fail each.

controls.reason: The capability inventory can omit uses, and whether a fallback is graceful is a contextual UX and safety judgment rather than an exact execution state.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted camera path prompts before explaining need and crashes on denial; listed geolocation cases pass permission and feature tests. The proposal passes while the full rule is false.

controls.reason: Finite orientation and viewport fixtures cannot prove continuity of every session, task, draft, focus position, and state, and continuity itself needs a complete oracle.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A long checkout preserves login in the test but loses an unsaved address after rotation. Approved fixtures pass while unrelated task state is destroyed.

controls.reason: `Verify` and `constrained sizes` lack objective visual or usability oracles, and approved examples can omit problematic content variants.
controls.counterexample_analysis: One short table and form pass at 320 pixels, but a long localized dialog clips its action buttons. The matrix passes while constrained-size behavior remains broken.

controls.reason: Event logs can omit signal sources, and a linked review record does not prove complaints and failures were substantively reviewed as design-quality evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Cancellation failures from a provider are unlogged, while other events create auto-closed review rows. All joins pass despite a missing signal and no meaningful design review.

controls.reason: Determining which experiments alter user autonomy and whether review is genuinely independent requires ethical and governance judgment; an experiment register can omit trials.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A coercive cancellation experiment is labelled ordinary growth and excluded, while listed autonomy experiments have formal reviews. The proposal passes despite the missing independent review.

controls.reason: This is an exact documentation requirement for four support dimensions, so a current authoritative matrix with complete rows fully decides it.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a browser without device class, an operating system without viewport bounds, and a stale matrix; each fails the schema or freshness checks. Journey success is outside this rule.

controls.reason: The critical-journey and support matrices can omit real critical flows or supported variants, and finite fixtures cannot prove each journey works in all relevant states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Checkout recovery on a supported small-screen browser is omitted while every declared happy-path combination passes. The proposal reports success although a critical supported journey is broken.

controls.reason: State names and passing fixtures do not prove every relevant screen has a meaningful design and exhaustive test for all eight states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted billing panel has no partial state, while the registered pages contain empty mockups and trivial tests for each state label. The composite passes despite missing design and behavior.

controls.reason: Correct navigation behavior depends on route, state, browser, authentication, and history context; an approved matrix can omit failing combinations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Refresh works in listed public routes, but a deep-linked authenticated modal loses state after back and forward. All declared cases pass while navigation behavior is not generally correct.

controls.reason: Critical-path scope and console-error materiality require judgment, while a bounded run cannot prove absence across all inputs, browsers, states, and timing.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted payment retry throws asynchronously, and a data-loss warning is classified nonmaterial. Every declared path has a clean console, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: `Where supported` lacks an independent capability predicate, and the scenario matrix can omit browsers, file types, permission states, and native integration paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Clipboard paste works in the approved desktop case, but file upload fails on a supported mobile browser omitted from the matrix. Every declared fixture passes.

controls.reason: The route policy can omit pages or encode a wrong public/private decision, so matching directives does not prove crawler rules are correct.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A private invoice preview is wrongly classified public and emits the approved index directive. All route comparisons pass while sensitive content can be indexed.

controls.reason: A private-data route inventory cannot enumerate alternate hosts, methods, objects, caches, files, and dynamically generated access paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A legacy document URL exposes a private file without authentication but is absent from the inventory. Every declared private route denies unauthenticated access, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The approved route matrix can omit outcomes or prescribe a semantically wrong status, and soft-error meaning depends on rendered content and crawler interpretation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A missing product returns a branded 200 page because the contract says 200; every listed fixture matches its status. The proposal passes despite a soft error.

controls.reason: Set equality with self-declared public and restricted URL inventories cannot prove those inventories include every generated, preview, temporary, or private URL.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A private preview URL is omitted from the restricted registry and included as public. The sitemap exactly matches the approved public set, so the proposal passes while exposing it.

controls.reason: No bounded inventory can prove removal from every application cache, CDN, browser, search engine, archive, provider snapshot, and indexing workflow.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A deleted profile remains in a regional CDN cache not listed by the project. Every inventoried cache and index reports removal, so the proposal passes while content remains exposed.

controls.reason: Environment discovery is incomplete and `unintentionally` depends on human intent; a declared environment can be omitted or deliberately mislabelled.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A forgotten preview hostname is indexed but absent from inventory, while another exposed test site is marked intentionally public. All declared environment rules pass.

controls.reason: Search and snapshot surfaces include external and provider-controlled copies that cannot be completely enumerated or synchronously observed after every access change.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A public snapshot service retains a now-private page outside the configured cache inventory. All declared caches invalidate correctly, so the universal privacy promise still fails.

controls.reason: Nonempty fields do not establish clear, coherent conflict, merge, retry, and synchronization behavior for every offline change and state transition.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The record says `retry` for all five topics and omits concurrent edits from one client. Required headings pass while actual offline conflict behavior is undefined.

controls.reason: Finite measurements cannot prove background synchronization stays within network, battery, storage, and compute limits across devices, duration, data sizes, retries, and failures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The job meets budgets in the fixture but loops after an intermittent outage on a low-memory phone. Approved runs pass while operational resource use is unbounded.

controls.reason: The statement requires an explicit model containing eight named states; a versioned state-machine record with those states and transitions decides that design fact.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried state labels without transitions, omitting permission, and using a model bound to another revision; each fails the explicit model schema. Runtime correctness is not asserted.

controls.reason: This is a documentation requirement for six named frontend behaviors, which current versioned sections with defined outcomes can prove completely.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a cache section without invalidation behavior, a missing logout outcome, and stale migration guidance; each fails topic or freshness validation. Correct implementation is separate.

controls.reason: A finite component-failure suite cannot prove that every failure mode is contained or that all unrelated user work survives every propagation path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The tested widget exception is contained, but an unlisted provider rejection crashes the app and erases an unrelated draft. All declared fault fixtures pass.

controls.reason: What components, complete journeys, and browsers are representative requires contextual selection, and approved matrices can omit the difficult combinations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The matrix tests two simple components and Chrome but omits a critical Safari payment journey. Every declared test executes while coverage is not representative.

controls.reason: Proving that no client check becomes a trusted boundary requires complete inventories of endpoints, actions, validations, authorization paths, and indirect backends.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted bulk endpoint trusts a client `isAdmin` flag. Every declared action is revalidated by the server, so the proposal passes while a client-side check remains authoritative.

controls.reason: Programmatic association can be parsed, but whether all needed instructions are visible, understandable, and associated requires accessibility judgment and complete form-control discovery.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A custom date field has a label node and ID but its required format is conveyed only by placeholder color; an unlisted shadow-DOM control lacks a label. Static checks pass.

controls.reason: The universal server-authority claim needs a complete input and endpoint inventory, while whether client validation gives timely assistance is a UX judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted import endpoint trusts client validation, and another field shows help only after submission. Declared endpoints reject invalid data, so the composite passes.

controls.reason: `Near` and `accessible summary` require spatial, semantic, focus, announcement, and assistive-technology judgment across every multi-field form.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The summary exists in the DOM but is not announced and the field message appears off-screen. Selector and distance fixtures pass while the failure is not accessibly communicated.

controls.reason: Valid input and recoverable failure are undefined across forms and workflows, and a finite fixture set cannot prove preservation for every field and failure path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A listed timeout preserves text, but an unlisted conflict response clears a valid uploaded file. Approved cases pass while valid input is lost after a recoverable failure.

controls.reason: Different error labels or enum values do not prove users can semantically distinguish six failure causes or receive the right recovery guidance.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All six errors have unique codes but render the same `Something went wrong` message. The state model passes while users cannot distinguish them.

controls.reason: The control asks for tests of seven named browser and network behaviors, so authenticated execution of an exact scenario for each proves occurrence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting multi-tab, using a client-only error instead of a server error, and evidence from another revision; category and binding checks fail each. Universal correctness is not claimed.

controls.reason: Whether budgets are user-centric and devices and networks are representative requires user and product judgment that numeric field presence cannot verify.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Budgets use a high-end laptop and unmetered fiber for a low-income mobile audience, yet every metric has a number. The schema passes without representative or user-centric budgets.

controls.reason: `Long` and `excessive` require policy thresholds and representative workload scope; bounded traces can omit pages, states, devices, and data volumes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The approved home-page trace meets limits, but a long-list view performs repeated layout on a supported phone. All declared measurements pass while excessive rendering remains.

controls.reason: Complete third-party inventory and privacy impact cannot be proven by runtime metrics, and failure and availability constraints need broader operational evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A tag manager injects an unlisted tracker that leaks identifiers and blocks rendering on outage. Listed scripts meet CPU and network budgets, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The statement requires tests in seven explicitly named performance states, not favorable performance; authenticated environment captures prove each test occurred.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried treating warm as returning-user, omitting degraded service, and reusing a stale run; distinct state metadata and revision binding reject each.

controls.reason: The proposal does not define the statistical protocol for meaningful deterioration or prove that linked investigation records contain genuine analysis and action.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A noisy one-run slowdown crosses an arbitrary threshold and creates an empty `investigated` row, while a real regression is hidden by aggregation. Fields pass without a sound investigation.

controls.reason: The change inventory can omit optimizations, and `end-to-end benefit` requires a causal metric, representative scope, and success threshold not supplied by generic evidence joins.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A cache tweak has a pre-profile and improves one lab metric but slows the complete checkout journey; all declared comparisons pass while end-to-end benefit is absent.

controls.reason: Numeric fixtures cannot prove telemetry overhead stays bounded across every device, session length, event burst, failure mode, and telemetry source.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The measured short session meets limits, but an error loop floods telemetry and exhausts storage after hours. All approved evidence passes while overhead becomes unbounded.

controls.reason: States, variants, boundaries, permissions, locales, themes, and responsive sizes lack independently complete inventories and some boundaries require semantic selection.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The matrix omits a permission-denied variant and a long translated boundary value. Every declared component case executes, so the proposal passes despite missing coverage.

controls.reason: The control requires test occurrence for seven named navigation and session categories, which exact authenticated executions can verify.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting multiple tabs, substituting reload for refresh and session change, and stale evidence; category identity and revision checks fail each. It does not claim every route works.

controls.reason: Six network-response conditions are explicitly enumerated, so controlled network fixtures and authenticated executions can prove each was simulated.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried latency without a failed response, duplication without reorder coverage, and a canceled request with no execution trace; the six-category matrix rejects each omission.

controls.reason: The statement is test occurrence for five named client-state behaviors; bound executions with distinct fixtures and expected outcomes decide it.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a retry test relabelled rollback, omitted cache invalidation, and results from an older artifact; exact scenario and artifact joins fail each.

controls.reason: The form inventory can omit controls and the international and long input domains, server rejection classes, and validity oracles are not exhaustively defined.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A listed text field passes eight simple fixtures, but an unlisted address form rejects a valid long international name. The matrix passes while forms are not fully verified.

controls.reason: A forbidden-call AST list cannot prove absence of indirect fixed delays, wrappers, aliases, busy waits, or dynamically selected timer APIs.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A helper `settle()` always waits five seconds but is not named as a sleep call. The syntax-aware scan finds no forbidden API and passes while tests still use a fixed sleep.
